paper_metadata.title: Q-A3C2: QUANTUM REINFORCEMENT LEARNING WITH TIME-SERIES DYNAMIC CLUSTERING FOR ADAPTIVE ETF STOCK SELECTION

summary: The paper proposes Q‑A3C2, a hybrid reinforcement learning model that inserts a variational quantum circuit into the policy network for ETF stock selection. Trained on S&P 500 data from Aug 2021–Aug 2024 and validated from Dec 2024–Aug 2025, the strategy reports a cumulative return of 17.09% versus a 7.09% S&P 500 benchmark. However, no quantum resource details or quantitative comparisons with the classical ablation models are reported.

experiments.description: Quantum-enhanced A3C ETF stock selection with time-series dynamic clustering, using a variational quantum circuit as a bottleneck in the policy network and compared against a classical MLP bottleneck and static/rolling clustering baselines.

algorithm.variant: Q-A3C2 with VQC bottleneck in A3C policy network
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 4,500 epochs; reward stabilized after approximately 2,000 epochs under relative-optimality reward

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical state vector St is processed by dense layers and then mapped into a variational quantum circuit VQC(xt; θ); the paper does not describe the feature map, qubit count, or specific encoding circuit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize monthly cluster-selection reward in an A3C reinforcement learning setup, where the selected cluster receives +1 if it has the highest next-month return and otherwise a bounded quadratic penalty based on relative return gap.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit hard constraints; cluster selection is handled through softmax policy over K clusters and reward shaping via relative-optimality reward.

problem_instance.description: Adaptive ETF stock selection over S&P 500 constituents using monthly rebalancing and time-series dynamic clustering.

dataset_specification.description: Daily closing prices of all S&P 500 constituent stocks; training from August 2021 to August 2024; validation from December 2024 to August 2025; benchmark is the S&P 500 index

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: For each stock and time t, compute 5-day cumulative return, 20-day cumulative return, and 20-day return volatility from the preceding L-day window; K-Means clustering applied to the feature matrix at each decision window; monthly portfolio rebalancing
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single training run described over 4,500 epochs; out-of-sample validation over 2024-12 to 2025-08; compared cumulative return against S&P 500 benchmark and against classical ablations/baselines

implementation_details.classical_solver: A3C with classical MLP bottleneck baseline; K-Means clustering; softmax policy sampling
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature construction from rolling return windows; K-Means clustering of stock features; monthly rebalancing environment
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Cumulative return comparison versus benchmark; monthly cluster-return analysis; selected-stock summaries

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: z-score reward unstable/oscillatory; relative-optimality reward stabilizes after ~2,000 epochs

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports improved cumulative return versus the S&P 500 benchmark, but does not claim or demonstrate computational speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified. The paper does not report qubit counts, circuit depth, gate counts, or scaling behavior needed to estimate resources for advantage.
limiting_factors: No quantum hardware execution; experiment appears to rely on classical simulation of a VQC.
No reported qubit count, circuit depth, or variational parameter count.
No quantitative comparison with the classical MLP bottleneck baseline despite describing it.
Performance improvement is measured only against a financial benchmark (S&P 500), not against classical algorithms solving the same RL problem.
No computational complexity analysis or scaling study.

notes: The paper explicitly states that a variational quantum circuit (VQC) is embedded in the policy network, but it does not report qubit count, circuit depth, gate counts, optimizer, or hardware/device details.
Classical baselines include a parameter-matched MLP bottleneck, static clustering, and rolling clustering without RL; these are not separate quantum experiments.
Authors report improved trading returns (17.09% vs 7.09% benchmark) but do not claim computational quantum advantage.
Because classical baselines are described but their results are not numerically reported, quantum vs classical performance cannot be assessed.
